message.content:
To terminate Visual Studio Code from the command line (Windows), you can use the built‑in **taskkill** utility:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

Explanation of the switches:

| Switch | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `/IM`  | Specifies the image name (process name) – here `code.exe`. |
| `/F`   | Forces termination (equivalent to “End Task” in Task Manager). |

If you only want to close a specific instance and not all VS Code windows, first find its Process ID (PID):

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

This will list all running `code.exe` processes along with their PIDs. Then kill the desired one:

```cmd
taskkill /PID <pid_number> /F
```

Replace `<pid_number>` with the actual PID you obtained.

---

### Quick cheat sheet

| Action | Command |
|--------|---------|
| List all VS Code processes | `tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"` |
| Kill all VS Code processes | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` |
| Kill a specific process by PID | `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` |

That’s it! Use the appropriate command depending on whether you want to close just one instance or all instances of VS Code.
